messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: The DOI and URL exactly match the citation information provided in the source metadata (Water Research 2021 205 117677, DOI: 10.1016/j.watres.2021.117677).

The abstract states the study is a field demonstration for "12 PFASs detected in groundwater impacted by aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF) at a U.S. Department of Defense installation" (S09-E02), matching the matrix description.

The abstract clearly supports that 12 PFASs were detected in groundwater impacted by AFFF (S09-E02). However, the provided text does not state that this suite included PFCAs, PFSAs, and PFAA precursors, so the class-level detail is not directly supported by the cited chunks.

The methods describe a "custom-built high-pressure membrane system" containing three 2540 spiral wound NF270 membranes used to treat 568 L batches of groundwater (S09-E03,E06), and figures/text refer to 30 days of operation (S09-E02,E04,E07). This supports a pilot-scale, three-element, 30-day field NF operation as described.
The work is described as a "field demonstration of a pilot-scale hybrid NF and UV-sulfite treatment train" (S09-E02), supporting classification as pilot_or_field_deployment.

The methods specify a custom-built high-pressure membrane system with three NF270 spiral-wound elements treating 568 L batches to 90% permeate recovery, yielding 57 L reject per cycle (S09-E03,E06). The abstract and methods describe it as part of a hybrid NF and UV-sulfite treatment train (S09-E01,E02,E04), matching the treatment description.

The study uses a commercial NF270 spiral-wound configuration (S09-E03), treats real AFFF-impacted groundwater at a DoD site (S09-E02), operates at defined flux (18.8 LMH) and recovery (90% total, 28% single-pass) (S09-E06), reports PFAS rejection over 30 days (S09-E02,E04,E07), and discusses fouling/permeability trends (S09-E04,E07). These details justify a status of comparable_with_conditions for other high-pressure membrane studies with matched operating points.

The reason accurately reflects the documented conditions: defined AFFF-impacted groundwater (S09-E02,E08), NF270 spiral-wound pilot system (S09-E03), specified flux and recovery (S09-E06), and reported PFAS rejection and fouling/permeability trends (S09-E02,E04,E07). It is a reasonable inference from the cited evidence.

The endpoint concerns NF rejection of PFASs, i.e., phase separation: the abstract reports NF rejection ≥95% for most detected PFASs at 90% recovery over a 30-day field trial (S09-E02), and S09-E04 notes field rejection values 92–98%. Classifying this as a separation endpoint is appropriate and supported.

The interpretation that NF270 effectively separated PFASs, achieving high rejection for most PFASs at 90% recovery over 30 days, is directly supported by the abstract ("NF rejection was consistently ≥ 95% over a 30-day field trial when operating at 90% total permeate recovery"; S09-E02) and the field rejection range 92–98% (S09-E04).

The cited text (S09-E04,E07) describes changes in membrane permeability / temperature-corrected specific flux over concentration cycles and attributes the decline to membrane fouling. This is a fouling/permeability performance endpoint, not sorption of PFAS to the membrane. Classifying the endpoint_type as "sorption" is not supported by the evidence.

S09-E04 reports a "small initial increase in membrane permeability, as represented by temperature corrected specific flux ... in the first 5 concentration cycles followed by small, but continuous decrease in the subsequent 25 concentration cycles" and notes this suggests fouling and that longer-term operation might benefit from modified operating conditions or cleaning protocols. This supports the stated interpretation of an initial increase then gradual decline indicating some fouling.

The abstract and methods indicate treatment of groundwater from a single AFFF-impacted DoD installation (S09-E02,E08). NF field operation and rejection trends are reported at 90% total permeate recovery with a fixed single-pass flux of 18.8 LMH and 28% single-pass recovery for all experiments (S09-E06), while the 30-day performance data and fouling discussion focus on 90% recovery (S09-E02,E04,E07). It is a reasonable design-inferred limitation that the main performance evaluation used one groundwater matrix and primarily one operating point.

S09-E04 states that the membrane cleaning protocol "consisted only of daily membrane system flushes for 15 min" and suggests longer-term operation might benefit from modified operating conditions or cleaning protocols. The figures and text refer to a 30-day operation period (S09-E02,E04,E07). It is therefore supported and reasonable to infer that fouling and long-term stability were evaluated over 30 days under a single, simple cleaning regime, with other strategies or longer durations untested.

S09-E03 describes the "custom-built high-pressure membrane system" containing "three 2540 (2.5” diameter × 40” length) spiral wound NF270 membranes (NF; DuPont Filmtec, Midland, MI)". This matches the stated membrane type and configuration.
No unit is appropriate for a descriptive membrane type/configuration field; the null unit is consistent with the qualitative nature of the value and the source description (S09-E03).
S09-E06 states: "All membrane experiments were operated at a conservative single pass permeate flux of 18.8 LMH". This directly supports the value 18.8 for single-pass permeate flux.
The unit for single-pass permeate flux is reported as LMH in S09-E06, matching the extracted unit.
S09-E06 specifies "28% single-pass recovery (approximately 6.3 LMH or 9.3% recovery per element...)". This supports a single-pass recovery value of 28.
Single-pass recovery is expressed as a percentage in S09-E06 ("28% single-pass recovery"), consistent with the % unit.
S09-E06 reports a "single-pass reject flowrate of 6.2 L/min". This directly supports the value 6.2.
The reject flowrate unit is explicitly given as L/min in S09-E06, matching the extracted unit.

S09-E03 and S09-E06 state that the system treated 568 L batches to "90% total permeate recovery (and yielding 57 L of reject)". This supports a total permeate recovery value of 90 under semi-batch operation.
Total permeate recovery is a percentage; the text refers to "90% total permeate recovery" (S09-E03,E06). The % unit is appropriate.
S09-E03 and S09-E06 note that the NF pilot "was used to treat 568 L batches of groundwater". This supports the batch volume per cycle value of 568.
The batch volume per cycle is expressed in liters in the source ("568 L batches of groundwater"; S09-E03,E06), matching the unit L.
S09-E03 and S09-E06 indicate that treatment of 568 L to 90% permeate recovery yielded "57 L of reject" per cycle, supporting the reject volume per cycle value of 57.
Reject volume is given in liters ("57 L of reject"; S09-E03,E06), so the L unit is correct.
S09-E06 notes each treatment cycle had a "~3.5 h treatment time". This supports the value 3.5 for treatment time per cycle.
Treatment time is explicitly given in hours ("~3.5 h"; S09-E06), matching the unit h.
S09-E06 states: "One treatment cycle was conducted per day during the field deployment." This directly supports a value of 1 cycle per day.
The phrase "One treatment cycle was conducted per day" (S09-E06) is consistent with the unit cycle/day.

S09-E03 describes pretreatment as sequential filtration through 50, 20, and 5 μm sediment filters followed by five cation exchange cartridge filters in series for removal of Ca2+ and Mg2+. This matches the extracted pretreatment description.
Pretreatment is described qualitatively; no numerical unit is appropriate. A null unit is consistent with the source (S09-E03).
S09-E04 states membrane cleaning protocols "consisted only of daily membrane system flushes for 15 min." This supports the description of daily flushes as the membrane cleaning practice.
Membrane cleaning is qualitatively described; no quantitative unit applies, so a null unit is suitable and consistent with S09-E04.
S09-E04 reports that "Rejection values observed in the field (92 – 98%)" were similar to lab results. The extracted range 92–98 and value_form=range align with this text.
The text gives rejection values as percentages ("92 – 98%"; S09-E04), matching the % unit.

S09-E04 states that a small initial increase in membrane specific flux was observed in the first 5 concentration cycles followed by a small, continuous decrease in the subsequent 25 cycles (for a total of 30 cycles), but it does not quantify this as a 5–30 day range or provide a numeric days interval for the trend. The extracted numeric range 5–30 is an inference not directly supported by the text and mixes cycles with time, so the specific value is not supported, even though the qualitative trend is.

The source describes changes over "the first 5 concentration cycles" and "the subsequent 25 concentration cycles" (S09-E04), not over a 5–30 day interval. The proper basis is cycles, not days, and no explicit time range is given. Using "days" as the unit is therefore not supported by the cited text.

S09-E03,E06 describe NF semi-batch operation concentrating 568 L to 57 L reject (a ~90% volume reduction, i.e., concentrating to ~10% of feed volume). S09-E04 and section 3.3 state that UV treatment was applied to PFASs that accumulated in the NF reject stream, i.e., the byproduct following 90% recovery. Combined with S09-E01, which positions NF/RO as separation steps and UV-sulfite as the destructive step, it is a reasonable, design-inferred statement that NF alone did not destroy PFASs and instead produced a concentrated reject subsequently treated by UV-sulfite.

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements—source identity, matrix (AFFF-impacted groundwater), NF270 membrane type and configuration, key operating conditions (flux, recovery, flowrate, batch and reject volumes, cycle timing), study scale, and main separation performance (PFAS rejection and fouling/permeability trend)—are all directly supported by the cited text. One endpoint is misclassified as sorption instead of fouling/permeability, and one quantitative finding (the 5–30 days range with a days unit) is not supported, but these issues do not compromise the core interpretability of the NF performance data for comparative review. The record is therefore usable with minor corrections needed for that endpoint classification and the unsupported quantitative trend metric.
